title: Localization Transition in Kinetically Deformed one-dimensional Aubry-André Model
abstract: We propose a $q$-deformation in the single-particle kinetic energy and investigate how it modifies the localization in the one-dimensional Aubry-André (AA) model. We construct a Hermitian $q$-deformed kinetic operator as a nonlinear function of the lattice translation operator, preserving the uniform lattice and recovering the conventional AA Hamiltonian continuously in the undeformed limit $q\to1$. The deformation generates an infinite set of correlated odd-range kinetic processes, controlled by a single parameter q, rather than phenomenologically involving long-range hopping. Under the dual transformation, this long-range hopping appears as higher harmonics of the dual quasiperiodic potential, providing a controlled route for breaking the exact self-duality of the AA model, with $q$ as the control parameter, consequently modifying the localization structure for $q\neq1$. In contrast to the conventional AA model, where all eigenstates localize simultaneously at $λ_c=2$, the deformed model exhibits a fraction of delocalized states even beyond $λ_c =2$. An intermediate regime also emerges in the $q-λ$ plane where localized and extended eigenstates coexist across the spectrum. We also propose a possible experimental realization of the hierarchy produced in the $q$-deformed kinetic setting in a periodically driven AA model.
summary: This work modifies the Aubry-André model by introducing a q-deformation into the kinetic energy term, controlled by the parameter q. This deformation generates an infinite, correlated set of long-range hopping terms, fundamentally altering the system's localization structure. The key finding is the emergence of a new intermediate phase where localized and extended eigenstates coexist, extending the physics beyond the model's original critical point.
main_problem: The paper investigates how introducing a q-deformation into the kinetic energy term of the one-dimensional Aubry-André (AA) model modifies the system's localization properties.
main_result: The deformation breaks the AA model's exact self-duality, leading to a fraction of delocalized states even beyond the standard critical point ($\lambda_c=2$) and creating an intermediate regime of coexisting localized and extended eigenstates.
method: The authors construct a Hermitian q-deformed kinetic operator using q-number algebra and analyze the resulting spectral properties using localization diagnostics like the Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR).
model_or_system: The system is the one-dimensional Aubry-André (AA) model, modified by a q-deformation in the single-particle kinetic energy. The Hamiltonian is $H_q = H_{kin}(q) + \lambda \cos(2\pi\alpha n + \phi)$, where $H_{kin}(q)$ is a nonlinear function of the lattice translation operator.
key_observables: Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), Normalized Participation Ratio (NPR), and the existence/location of delocalized states.
important_parameters: Deformation parameter $q$, potential strength $\lambda$, and the critical point $\lambda_c=2$.
main_assumptions: The deformation is controlled by the single parameter $q$, which generates an infinite, correlated hierarchy of odd-range hopping processes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the localization map (D, M, L phases) in the $q-\lambda$ plane, the correlated odd-range hopping amplitudes, and the convergence of IPR/NPR diagnostics with system size $N$.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the $q$-deformation, derives the resulting infinite-range hopping structure, analyzes the breakdown of self-duality, and finally maps out the modified localization phase diagram compared to the standard AA model.
why_interesting: The study provides a controlled, algebraic mechanism (q-deformation) to perturb a fundamental model in condensed matter physics, allowing for the exploration of novel spectral phases (coexistence of localized/extended states) beyond standard critical points.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Numerically determined localization map to the q-generalized AA model. D = delocalized phase, M = mixed (intermediate) phase, and L = Localized phase. The c1 and c2 lines correspond to the D-M and M-L crossover lines in the phase diagram.

FIG. 2: (a) Normalized odd-range hopping amplitudes |tr/t1| generated by the q-deformed kinetic operator. The higher range processes are not independently tunable but are correlated through the single deformation parameter q. (b) Corresponding group velocity vq(k) = ∂εq(k)/∂k. The deformation progressively modifies the velocity’s momentum dependence, shifting it away from the sinusoidal form of the conventional nearest-neighbor model. These two representations provide complementary views of the same kinetic deformation.

FIG. 3: Average IPR as a function of q and λ. The red dashed line corresponds to λ = 2. The q is varied from 0.1 to 2 and λ is varied from 0 to 4. q = 1 gives back the standard AA limit. Calculations are done for N = 1000.
FIG. 4: The contour plot of IPR of each state as a function of energy (E) and quasi-periodic potential strength for (a) q = 0.5 and (b) q = 2.5 for system size N = 1000.
FIG. 5: ⟨IPR⟩, ⟨NPR⟩as a function of λ at (a) q = 0.5 and (b) q = 2.5 respectively for system size N = 1000.
